mcq.q: In a 4x1 MUX, with S1 = 1 and S0 = 0 (standard convention, S1 is the most significant select bit), which input is passed to the output?
mcq.explanation: S1S0 = 10 is binary 2, so I2 is selected. (The slide table lists S0 first; check your teacher convention.)

mcq.q: A 8x1 MUX needs how many select lines?
mcq.explanation: 2^3 = 8, so 3 select lines.

mcq.q: In a 1x4 DEMUX with select lines S1S0 = 11, the output that becomes active is:
mcq.explanation: S1S0 = 11 is binary 3, so Y3 gets the input.

mcq.q: A 2x4 decoder has how many output lines?
mcq.explanation: 2 inputs give 2^2 = 4 outputs.

mcq.q: A decoder with input 101 (3 bits) activates which output in a 3x8 decoder?
mcq.explanation: Binary 101 = decimal 5, so output 5 is activated.

mcq.q: An 8x3 encoder has:
mcq.explanation: Encoder has 2^n inputs and n outputs; for n = 3, 8 inputs and 3 outputs.

mcq.q: In a 4-bit SISO shift register, how many clock pulses are needed to shift a 4-bit serial word in fully?
mcq.explanation: One bit is shifted in per clock pulse, so 4 pulses are needed.

mcq.q: A register that loads all bits at once and gives output bit by bit is:
mcq.explanation: Parallel In Serial Out (PISO).

mcq.q: A 3-bit binary counter has how many distinct states?
In a synchronous counter, the flip-flops are driven by:
options: The output of the last flip-flop only
mcq.explanation: All flip-flops share one clock in a synchronous counter.

mcq.q: Which counter is also called a ripple counter?
mcq.explanation: Asynchronous counters are called ripple counters because the carry ripples from stage to stage.

mcq.q: A 16-bit register is built from how many flip-flops?
mcq.explanation: One flip-flop per bit, so 16.

mcq.q: An IC with 10 to 200 gates is classified as:
mcq.explanation: MSI (Medium Scale Integration).

mcq.q: A chip with more than 1 million transistors is classified as:
mcq.explanation: ULSI (Ultra Large Scale Integration) has more than 1 million transistors.

mcq.q: Which is an application of counters?
mcq.explanation: Counters are used in digital clocks, watches, pulse generators and alarm systems.

mcq.q: Which device sends one input line to one of many output lines?
mcq.explanation: DEMUX is one to many.

mcq.q: A MUX with 16 inputs requires how many select lines?
mcq.explanation: 2^4 = 16, so 4 select lines.

mcq.q: Binary to hexadecimal conversion uses which decoder?
mcq.explanation: Hex needs 16 outputs from 4 bits.

mcq.q: In a bidirectional shift register, data can be shifted:
mcq.explanation: A bidirectional shift register can shift left or right.

mcq.q: Advantage of synchronous counters over asynchronous counters is:
mcq.explanation: All flip-flops change together, so they are faster.

mcq.q: In the 8x3 encoder, output X is equal to:
mcq.explanation: From the slide circuit: X = D4+D5+D6+D7.

mcq.q: In the 8x3 encoder, output Z is equal to:
mcq.explanation: From the slide circuit: Z = D1+D3+D5+D7.

mcq.q: In the 8x3 encoder, when input D0 is active, the output XYZ is:
mcq.explanation: D0 is not part of any output equation, so the outputs are 000 for D0.

mcq.q: Which device is said to have the most common component as NAND, NOR or inverter gate?
mcq.explanation: The slide says the most common component in VLSI technology is NAND, NOR or inverter.

mcq.q: Another name of synchronous counter is:
mcq.explanation: A synchronous counter is also called a simultaneous counter.

mcq.q: In the 1x4 DEMUX truth table on the slide, the select lines are written as S1 then S0. With S1 = 0 and S0 = 1 and D = 1, which output is 1?
mcq.explanation: S1S0 = 01 selects F1.

short.q: Explain the working of a 4x1 multiplexer with select lines S1 = 1, S0 = 0 (standard convention).
short.answer: Binary 10 selects input I2, so the output Y equals I2.

short.q: Draw the basic idea of a 1x4 DEMUX and state how many select lines it uses.
short.answer: One input line D goes to one of four outputs Y0 to Y3 chosen by the two select lines S1 and S0; it uses 2 select lines.

short.q: How many outputs does a 3x8 decoder have and why?
short.answer: 8 outputs, because 3 input lines can represent 2^3 = 8 different codes.

short.q: Differentiate between an encoder and a decoder.
short.answer: A decoder has n inputs and 2^n outputs and activates one output for each input code. An encoder has 2^n inputs and n outputs and produces the binary code of the active input. Encoder is the reverse of decoder.

short.q: Name the four shift register types and give one example use for SIPO.
short.answer: SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO. SIPO converts serial data into parallel form, e.g. a serial-to-parallel converter.

short.q: Give the number of flip-flops and the number of states for a 4-bit binary counter.
Why is an asynchronous counter slower than a synchronous counter?
short.answer: In an asynchronous counter each flip-flop is clocked by the previous one, so changes ripple through stage by stage, causing a delay.

short.q: Classify an IC that has 1000 to 10,000 gates and give an example.
Write the output equations of the 8x3 encoder for X, Y and Z.
List two advantages and one disadvantage of synchronous counters.
short.answer: Advantages: simple to design (compared to asynchronous), works simultaneously, no propagation delay, faster operation. Disadvantage: needs large components and complex logic as number of states increases (any valid answer).
